questions.text: What is the primary purpose of a scan chain in DFT?
options: A. To increase the clock frequency of a design
B. To provide sequential controllability and observability of flip-flops
C. To reduce power consumption during normal operation
D. To eliminate combinational logic hazards

questions.text: In scan design, what are the two operating modes of a scan flip-flop?
options: A. Read mode and Write mode
B. Normal (functional) mode and Shift (test) mode
C. Setup mode and Hold mode
D. Capture mode and Launch mode

questions.text: Which pin on a scan flip-flop selects between functional data and scan data?
options: A. SDI (Scan Data In)
B. SDO (Scan Data Out)
C. SE (Scan Enable)
D. SCK (Scan Clock)

questions.text: What is 'fault coverage' in the context of DFT?
options: A. The percentage of nets covered by routing tools
B. The ratio of detected faults to total modeled faults, expressed as a percentage
C. The number of scan chains in a design
D. The area overhead introduced by scan insertion

questions.text: Which fault model assumes a net is permanently stuck at logic '0' or logic '1'?
options: A. Transition Delay Fault (TDF) model
B. Bridging Fault model
C. Stuck-At Fault (SAF) model
D. Path Delay Fault model

questions.text: What is the key advantage of using multiple scan chains instead of a single long chain?
options: A. It eliminates the need for Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG)
B. It reduces routing complexity to zero
C. It shortens test application time by loading/unloading chains in parallel
D. It removes the need for a scan enable signal

questions.text: What does ATPG stand for and what is its role in DFT?
options: A. Automatic Timing and Power Guard — optimizes power during test
B. Automatic Test Pattern Generation — creates stimulus vectors to detect faults
C. Advanced Technology Process Guidelines — defines fabrication rules
D. Asynchronous Transfer Protocol Generator — manages test data transfer

questions.text: During a standard stuck-at scan test, what is the correct sequence of operations for one test cycle?
options: A. Capture → Shift-in → Apply clock → Shift-out
B. Shift-in pattern → Apply functional clock (capture) → Shift-out response
C. Reset → Scan-out → Apply stimulus → Scan-in
D. Launch → Shift-in → Capture → Compare

questions.text: What is 'scan compression' (also called EDT — Embedded Deterministic Test)?
options: A. A technique to physically compress the scan flip-flops into a smaller area
B. A method that uses on-chip decompressor/compactor logic to reduce test data volume and test time
C. A power gating scheme applied during scan shifting
D. A post-silicon debug feature for compressing waveforms

questions.text: Which DFT structure is commonly used to test embedded memories (SRAMs/ROMs) that cannot be adequately tested by scan logic alone?
options: A. Boundary Scan (JTAG)
B. Built-In Self-Test (BIST) — specifically MBIST (Memory BIST)
C. Transition Delay Fault ATPG
D. Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) checkers
